data.name: Skim Milk Powder
data.narrative:
Skim milk powder (SMP) prices increased at both ends of the range this reporting period, with gains at the upper end outpacing those at the lower end. Processor prices were up from both last month and year-ago levels, with a 60 percent improvement year-over-year (YoY). Futures trading volumes decreased slightly last week compared to the week prior. SMP futures were steady for November and April contract periods, but slightly lower for December through March contracts. A major New Zealand dairy cooperative maintained its projected total SMP offerings for the next 12 months. September trade data from the U.S. highlights weak demand from Australia/Oceania, with SMP exports down 68 percent since September 2025.

SMP prices at Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 416 increased across all offered contract periods, reaching their highest rolling 12-month average and highest platform average price since June 2022. No product was offered for April or May. January and February accounted for 80 percent of total sales. Total volume sold was lower than both Event 415 and year-earlier levels. North Asia was the top buyer, purchasing 52 percent of the total volume, up from 39 percent at the previous event but down from 63 percent a year ago. Southeast Asia/Oceania followed with 34 percent. The SMP average price is 65 percent higher YoY and continues to trade at a premium to whole milk powder.

data.name: Whole Milk Powder
data.narrative:
Whole milk powder (WMP) prices moved higher across the full range, with the largest gain at the bottom this reporting period. Processor prices increased from last month and are 14 percent higher than year-ago levels. Futures trading volumes decreased 19 percent last week compared to the week prior. WMP futures strengthened for all contract periods, increasing by as much as 2.3 percent for December. A major New Zealand dairy cooperative reported that the forecast total offer volume for WMP over the next 12 months remains unchanged.

WMP prices at Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 416 increased across all contract periods offered and the average price reached its highest level since June 2025. The February contract saw the largest increase, up 3.7 percent. No product was offered for April or May. January and February accounted for 76 percent of total sales. Sales volumes were slightly higher than Event 415, but lower than year-earlier levels. North Asia was the top buyer, purchasing 64 percent of the volume, down from 73 percent at the previous auction and up from 52 percent a year ago. Southeast Asia/Oceania bought 23 percent of the volume, followed by the Middle East. The WMP average price is 18 percent higher than a year ago but continues to trade at a discount to skim milk powder over the past several events.

data.name: Cheddar Cheese
data.narrative:
Cheddar cheese prices declined across the entire range this reporting period, with the largest loss at the lower end. Processor prices were higher than the previous month but remain 10 percent below year-ago levels. A major New Zealand dairy cooperative maintained its projected total cheddar offerings for the next 12 months. United States September trade data highlights weak demand from Australia/Oceania, with cheese exports 48 percent below September 2025 levels.

At Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 416, cheddar prices were mixed across all offered contract periods, with near-term contracts declining while longer-term contracts posted gains. The April contract recorded the largest increase, rising 4.5 percent. No cheddar was offered for the May contract. January and February accounted for 65 percent of all cheddar sales. Sales volumes were similar to Event 415 and year-ago levels. North Asia led purchasing, followed by Africa and the Middle East.

data.name: Butter
data.narrative: Butter prices decreased at both ends of the range, with the biggest drop at the bottom this reporting period. Processor prices decreased compared to last month and remain down 29 percent year-over-year (YoY). Futures trading volumes were higher last week compared to the week prior. Last week butter futures were lower across all months from November through April, led by the December contract, which fell nearly 8 percent. A major New Zealand dairy cooperative increased its forecast total offer quantity for butter for the next 12 months by 5,000 metric tons (MT) to 55,535 MT.Ample cream availability continues to drive milkfat markets lower, creating oversupply pressure and contributing to some of the sharpest price declines in recent history. While product continues to move through the market, excess supply is expected to keep prices under pressure in the near term. Trade data indicates abundant butter supplies globally, supported by strong production growth in Europe, the United States, Argentina, and New Zealand. United States September trade data highlights weak demand from Australia/Oceania, with butter exports down 65 percent since September 2025.At Global Dairy Trade (GDT) Event 416, butter prices were lower, with March losing the most ground, down 9.3 percent. No butter was offered for April or May. January and February accounted for 83 percent of total sales. Butter volume sold increased compared to Event 415 and year-ago levels. North Asia led purchasing with 75 percent, followed by Southeast Asia/Oceania and the Middle East.
